title: Two Girls by Eliya Smith at The Cherry Lane Theatre #twogirls #verbat...
transcript: Who knew a viral shock-p*rn video would be such ripe subject matter for a verbatim theatre piece? This often funny, sometimes awkward, and occasionally profound two-hander by Eliya Smith starts as an attempt to reconstruct the infamous Two Girls One Cup video, strictly through descriptions from men who remember seeing it back in the day. At first, we see a series of these conversations with no context. The way the piece reveals itself in how and why it was created is perfectly paced and compelling from start to finish. A personal connection for the playwright eventually emerges as well, revealing a meditation on the twisted relationship between disgust and desire, as it relates to the female body. I wish it could have gone a little deeper, but I understand the inherent limitations that come from making a verbatim piece. I was also plenty entertained by the performances from Chloe Claudel and Juliana Sass, and I've wondered how their characterizations compare to the cadence and pacing of the original conversations. For an hour-long show, there's a lot to chew on. Two Girls is running at The Cherry Lane through November 29th.
